title: One index on (customer_id, created_at): a fast range, a query it cannot help, and a covering index
captions: The index keeps one entry per row, sorted by customer_id first. Inside one customer, entries are sorted by created_at. Each entry also points to its row in the table.
Query A gives an exact customer and a start date. All its matches sit next to each other. The database jumps to the first one and reads until the range ends.
Query B gives only a date. The dates are sorted only inside each customer, so the matches are spread across the whole index. The database usually reads the whole table instead.
Query A also wants status and total. Those columns are not in the index. So for each match, Postgres must visit the table, called the heap, to read the row.
Add the two columns with INCLUDE. Now the index holds everything A needs. Postgres can answer from the index alone, if the table pages are marked all-visible.
